entries.content:
When pressed into a situation demanding blind obedience, I felt the heavy burden of duty—order must be preserved, yes, that’s what we’re told. Yet when the pain became clear, I found I simply could not continue, not if I wish to look my children in the eye and call myself nurturing; sometimes the hardest part of keeping a good home is knowing when obedience turns cruel. I feel justified in refusing, though a kernel of regret lingers—obedience can so easily become an excuse for abdicating the responsibility to protect, to temper harsh instruction with mercy, just as a good wife does when she must quietly weigh duty against what is right for those in her care.
